name: Cat Ba: Ngu Lam peak (Đỉnh Ngự Lâm)
region: Cat Ba National Park, Cat Ba Island, Hai Phong
why: A short, steep climb through the Kim Giao forest to an observation tower above the karst hills in the middle of Cat Ba Island.
book: Pay the small park entrance fee at the national park headquarters on the Hung Son road, in the middle of the island north-west of Cat Ba town (motorbike or taxi). No guide is needed for this trail.
water: No shops on the trail: carry 1-1.5 litres; drinks are sold at the headquarters.
dangers: Rock and stone steps are slippery and muddy after rain.
Heat and humidity from May to September: start early.
The top of the watchtower is exposed: hold the rail, and stay off it in a thunderstorm.
turnaround: In rain or thunder, stop at the Kim Giao viewpoint and go back down.

points.name: Cat Ba National Park gate and headquarters
points.note: Ticket office, information board and a small café by the Hung Son road. The trail heads east past the botanical garden into the forest.

points.name: Kim Giao viewpoint
points.note: Stone benches in the Kim Giao forest, named after its native podocarp trees. The last stretch to Ngu Lam is the steepest.

points.name: Ngu Lam peak watchtower
points.note: About 220 m. An observation tower over the forested karst hills of the island; a good lunch stop. Return the same way.
